oneLiner.en: The Rav speaks about bringing lost Jewish souls back to Hashem, Hashem's complaint against those who did not bring back the one who strayed, and the principle that among Jews nothing is ever beyond hope.

abstract.en: Most of this recording is barely intelligible, so only the outline of the shiur can be followed. The catalog describes a talk on chinuch: returning lost souls to Hashem as a kind of returning a lost object, the role of individual educators, Hashem's complaint in Yechezkel against teachers who are not faithful, and never giving up hope on a Jewish soul. In the audible stretches the Rav speaks of souls that are lost and of the one who strayed and was not brought back, in connection with people who went away from the tzaddikim. At the end he states that among Jews there is no such thing as saying that something cannot be, and that a Jew is never written off.

en: The Rav speaks of Jewish souls that are lost to Hashem and need to be brought back.
He describes a complaint against those who did not bring back the one who strayed, when people went away from the tzaddikim.
He concludes that among Jews one can never say that something cannot be.

catalogTitle: חבורות: נחיצות לימוד ספרי חסידות שנתגלה להאיר בתוך חשכות זמננו של עיקבתא דמשיחא

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that in the darkness of ikvesa d'Meshicha the Torah of the Ba'al Shem Tov and his talmidim is the remedy Hashem sent for this era, and urges learning chassidic seforim, especially on Shabbos.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the Gemara's demand for 'emunah yeseirah', an extra measure of faith, and explains that Amalek fights emunah differently in every generation, and hardest now, as Moshiach nears. He describes the signs of the times: a collapsing world economy and the danger surrounding Eretz Yisrael, which can only be met with miracles. Yaakov saved his greatest brachos for the time of 'kol goyim sevavuni', and Malachi's 'az nidberu yirei Hashem' shows that the remedy is to gather and strengthen one another. He then shows how Hashem sent the Ba'al Shem Tov as the cure for haskalah, since every era receives what it needs, as Purim and the Megillah came with hester panim. Through R' Shlomo of Lutzk, the Degel and other sources he describes the Besht's greatness, and contrasts the loving voice of chassidic seforim with the rebuke of earlier mussar. He closes by urging Shabbos learning of chassidic seforim.

en: Every Jew has emunah, but the Gemara demands emunah yeseirah, and emunah has endless levels.
Amalek's war against emunah changes its tactics in every generation, and in the time before Moshiach he fights with all his strength because he sees his end coming.
The present situation of the world and of Eretz Yisrael is that of 'kol goyim sevavuni', the time for which Yaakov saved his greater brachos.
Hashem sent the Ba'al Shem Tov and Chassidus as the remedy for the haskalah; where Chassidus spread, haskalah did not succeed.
Each era receives from Hashem what it needs, and the Torah of the Besht is the new necessity of this era, a foretaste of the Torah of Moshiach.
Chassidic seforim speak to the soul with love, as Malachi does, and this is how one must speak to the broken Jews of today.
The Rav urges that besides mussar there should be a 'Shabbos-dik' learning, with groups learning chassidic seforim on Shabbos and Friday night.

title.en: Emunah yeseirah and Amalek's war in every generation

summary.en: The Rav opens with the Gemara that one should hold on to emunah yeseirah, explains that faith has endless levels, and that Amalek fights it with new tactics in each generation, hardest now before Moshiach. He adds that avodas Hashem cannot be routine; yiras Hashem must be sought like hidden treasure, as earlier generations did.

title.en: Signs of the times and the danger to Eretz Yisrael

summary.en: The Rav says there is no doubt this is the time before Moshiach: the world economy is collapsing as the Gemara's signs describe, and Eretz Yisrael is surrounded by enemies arming themselves. He recalls the miracles of the Six Day War and says today's situation can only be met with miracles.

title.en: Yaakov's brachos saved for 'kol goyim sevavuni'

summary.en: The Rav brings the Zohar that Yaakov received four brachos but used only the weakest against Esav, saving the other three for the time of 'kol goyim sevavuni', which he says is today. He then brings Daniel's prophecy of an 'eis tzarah' unlike any before.

title.en: The book of Malachi: 'az nidberu yirei Hashem'

summary.en: The Rav asks which 'book' Daniel means by those 'written in the book', and brings the seforim that it is Malachi's 'sefer zikaron' for those who fear Hashem and speak to one another. Malachi, the last prophet, speaks to the last generation, and the talmidim of the Besht taught that the only counsel before Moshiach is to gather and strengthen each other.

title.en: The Ba'al Shem Tov as the cure for haskalah

summary.en: The Rav describes how haskalah, communism and Zionism tore away large parts of Klal Yisrael, and how Hashem sent the Ba'al Shem Tov as the remedy, as He sent the end of prophecy against Greek philosophy. Where Chassidus spread, haskalah failed; today chassidic seforim are learned even in Litvish yeshivos, and each generation has its own changes.

title.en: Each era receives what it needs: the Megillah

summary.en: The Rav explains that Hashem's program runs through eras, each with its own way of learning and paskening, and each sent what it needs. His example is the Gemara on the Megillah: before Purim it was not needed, but in the new era of hester panim one cannot be a Jew without it, and it brought a new kind of Torah of 'kiymu v'kiblu'.

title.en: The new era of the Besht and R' Shlomo of Lutzk's testimony

summary.en: The Rav says a new era began with the Ba'al Shem Tov, a new way of avodah through love like that of Rashbi in the Zohar. He reads from R' Shlomo of Lutzk's introduction about the Maggid's greatness, his gilui Eliyahu, and what the Besht taught him: the speech of birds and trees, holy names and the angels of each month.

title.en: The Besht crossing the river with emunah

summary.en: The Rav tells from the Degel Machaneh Ephraim how the Besht crossed a dangerous river on his gartel, not through holy names but through simple emunah. He adds the Belzer tradition that every frum Jew even in Germany exists by the Besht's power, and that his talmidim called the Toldos Yaakov Yosef the Torah of Moshiach, a 'preview' of what will be learned then.

title.en: Speaking to the soul with love, as Malachi does

summary.en: The Rav describes how the Besht raised simple Jews to great levels, and brings the Ramchal on Moshe's 'shavisa shevi', a captive soul later identified with Rashbi, the Arizal and the Besht. He contrasts mussar seforim that teach through fear with the Besht's way of love: Yeshayahu opens with harsh rebuke, but Malachi, who speaks to the last generation, opens with 'ahavti eschem'.

title.en: Chassidic seforim on the greatness of Shabbos and mitzvos

summary.en: The Rav says chassidic seforim speak of the praises of Jewish children, as in the Berditchever's zemiros, and of the greatness of Shabbos, Yom Tov, tefillah and mitzvos, which other seforim hardly address; the Pri Tzaddik speaks of Shabbos in almost every Torah. This warmed and comforted Jews worn out by a week of hard labor, and he notes that Shlomo HaMelech wrote mussar seforim too.

title.en: Shir HaShirim and a call for Shabbos learning

summary.en: The Rav calls Shir HaShirim, the song of love between Hashem and Klal Yisrael, the crowning work of Shlomo HaMelech, and says chassidic seforim draw from it. He gives his advice: alongside mussar, learn in a Shabbos-dik way that comforts Jews whose blackness is only external, and form groups to learn chassidic seforim on Shabbos and Friday night.

catalogTitle: ברכת החמה: יתפלל שרק ה' יהיה אור של בנ"י ויתגלה שהשפע שייך רק להם

oneLiner.en: On the day of Birchas HaChamah the Rav explains that the sun's power of giving, which in exile seems to belong to Esav, truly belongs to Klal Yisroel, and that blessing the sun is a prayer that Hashem alone become Yisroel's light.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the teaching that the moon was given to Yisroel and the sun to the nations, and asks why Jews rejoice so much over a blessing on the sun. Citing the Toras Yeshaya on Rashi's first comment, he explains that Bereishis alludes to the sun and nature, and that every twenty-eight years Hashem wishes to hand the power of giving to Yisroel. From Rashi on Toldos he shows that Esav's greatness is borrowed from Yaakov. The blessing 'oseh maaseh bereishis' asks Hashem to return to the hidden light of creation, when no sun or moon was needed. He tells from the Bnei Yissaschar how the Chozeh of Lublin wrote down each month's events in the first twelve days of Nissan, notes the good sign that this year's blessing falls on the fourth of Nissan, the day of Tammuz, and calls for renewal, a cheshbon hanefesh and acceptance of Hashem's kingship.

en: The moon was given to Klal Yisroel and the sun to the nations, so some questioned why Jews rejoice so much over a blessing on the sun.
The sun is the giver and the moon the receiver; every twenty-eight years Hashem wishes to hand the sun's power of giving over to Klal Yisroel.
Esav's power is filled only from Yerushalayim's destruction, so in truth both the sun and the moon belong to Yaakov.
The blessing 'oseh maaseh bereishis' asks Hashem to bring back the hidden light of creation, when Hashem Himself, not the sun and moon, gives light.
The first twelve days of Nissan contain the whole year, and how a person conducts himself in them shapes his whole year.
This year the blessing falls on the fourth of Nissan, which corresponds to Tammuz, the month of the sun's dominion and of the churban, and the Rav sees this as a good sign.
Every twenty-eight years a person should renew himself and return to the upright state in which Hashem created him.

title.en: Why rejoice over the sun?

summary.en: The Rav notes that the moon was given to Yisroel and the sun to the nations, and asks why the blessing on the sun is a great simcha. He brings the Toras Yeshaya on Rashi's first comment: Bereishis alludes to the sun, the giver, and every twenty-eight years Hashem wishes to hand that power to Yisroel.

title.en: Esav's borrowed light and the hidden light

summary.en: From Rashi on Toldos the Rav shows that Esav's power comes only from Yerushalayim's destruction, so sun and moon both belong to Yaakov. He explains 'oseh maaseh bereishis' as a request to return to the hidden light of creation, and reads Rashi on 'me'oros' to show that needing luminaries to give light is a lack.

title.en: The Chozeh of Lublin's Nissan writings

summary.en: The Rav tells, from the Bnei Yissaschar's own testimony, how the Chozeh of Lublin wrote down in the first twelve days of Nissan everything that would happen in each month of the year. He explains that these days contain the whole year, so a person's conduct in them shapes his year.

title.en: The fourth of Nissan against Tammuz

summary.en: The Rav calls it a good sign that the blessing falls on the fourth of Nissan, corresponding to Tammuz, the month of the sun's strength and of the churban. Since a mitzvah Jews do with something puts strength into it, blessing the sun on that day is a sign that Esav's power will be taken away and the sun revealed as serving Yisroel.

title.en: Nissan renewal and the upright man

summary.en: The Rav describes Nissan as the month when everything blossoms and Klal Yisroel grows into a people ready for the Torah. He calls for a cheshbon hanefesh in the first twelve days, and says that every twenty-eight years a person should return to the upright state in which he was created and fit himself into the order of creation.

title.en: Accepting Hashem's kingship and closing brachos

summary.en: The Rav speaks of renewing oneself and accepting the kingship of Hashem, calls the day a simcha shel mitzvah and a time of favor for prayer, and closes with prayers for a refuah and that, as they merited to bless the sun, they merit a new light on Tzion and to sanctify the moon in Yerushalayim.

catalogTitle: Why ל”ג בעומר is the עיקר day of ספירה

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that Sefirah and the month of Iyar are a time for achdus, for joining opposites into the harmony of Tiferes, and that Lag BaOmer, Hod sheb'Hod, is Tiferes sheb'Tiferes when counted from Hashem's side, the day of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai who binds all Jews together.

abstract.en: The Rav opens by asking why Parshas Kedoshim was said to all of Klal Yisrael together. He describes the 600,000 souls as the letters of the Sefer Torah, rising from letters to words, families and shevatim up to the Avos and Yerushalayim, where every Jew is joined to every other. The third week of Sefirah is Tiferes, the harmony that blends opposites such as chesed and gevurah, and the Tomer Devorah calls Torah Tiferes and every machlokes a blemish in it. Counted from Hashem's side, Lag BaOmer is Tiferes sheb'Tiferes. He then explains why sedras are combined at four times of the year: to repair sinas chinam, rooted in the strife of Yehuda and Yosef and in the diminishing of the moon. In a leap year the moon catches up with the sun, so no combining is needed. He ends with Iyar and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, who unite all Jews, and with v'ahavta l'rei'acha kamocha.

en: The 600,000 Jewish souls are the letters of the Sefer Torah; they join into words, families and shevatim, up to the Avos, who contain all of Klal Yisrael.
On the Regalim a Jew is raised above his shevet to the level of the Avos, and in Yerushalayim, which belongs to no single shevet, all Jews are united.
Tiferes is harmony: two opposites, like chesed and gevurah, blended into a new and beautiful whole, and it is the main middah of Sefirah because Torah is Tiferes.
Counting from Malchus sheb'Malchus, Hashem's direction, Lag BaOmer is Tiferes sheb'Tiferes.
Sedras are combined at four times of the year to repair sinas chinam, which destroyed the Beis HaMikdash, the place of achdus.
The strife between Yehuda and Yosef goes back to the diminishing of the moon, and in a leap year, when the moon catches up with the sun, the sedras need not be combined.
Iyar and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai bind all Jews together, and Parshas Kedoshim, with v'ahavta l'rei'acha kamocha, was said when all of Klal Yisrael was gathered.

candidateTopics: sinas chinam and the beis hamikdash

title.en: Kedoshim b'hakhel and the letters of the Torah

summary.en: The Rav asks what is special about Parshas Kedoshim, which Rashi says was said to all the Jews together, and speaks of Shabbos Mevarchim and Iyar, the month of Sefirah. He describes the 600,000 souls as the letters of the Sefer Torah, from Moshe Rabbeinu down to the forgotten Jew.

title.en: From letters to shevatim, Avos and Yerushalayim

summary.en: The Rav traces how individual letters join into words, families and shevatim, up to the Avos, and shows the same order in Eretz Yisrael, where Yerushalayim belongs to no single shevet. On the Regalim a Jew rises to the Avos, and the Yerushalmi treats every Jew in Yerushalayim as a chaver.

title.en: Tiferes as harmony of opposites

summary.en: Entering the week of Tiferes, the Rav defines Tiferes as harmony: Yaakov merges the opposites of Avraham's chesed and Yitzchak's gevurah, like colors in a painting, husband and wife, or notes in a niggun. Citing the Tomer Devorah that Torah is Tiferes, he says Tiferes is the main middah of Sefirah.

title.en: Lag BaOmer as Tiferes sheb'Tiferes

summary.en: The Rav explains why Lag BaOmer is the noted day of Sefirah: Shavuos is the marriage of Hashem and Klal Yisrael, and as the chassan goes out toward the kallah, Hashem counts from Malchus upward, so Hod sheb'Hod is Tiferes sheb'Tiferes. He brings the Tomer Devorah that every machlokes blemishes Tiferes except a machlokes l'shem shamayim, which ends in greater shalom.

title.en: Why sedras are combined four times a year

summary.en: The Rav brings the Magen Avraham, from the Zohar, that sedras may not be mixed because each Shabbos and its sedra belong to a particular group of Jews, and asks why we nevertheless combine sedras at four times of the year. He answers that the Beis HaMikdash, the place of achdus, was destroyed by sinas chinam, so before Nisan, before Tishrei, in Sefirah and in the Three Weeks the barriers between Jews are broken.

title.en: Yehuda and Yosef: shlishi against shishi

summary.en: The Rav describes the two lines of leadership in Jewish history, Yehuda and Yosef, whose strife goes back to the kitrug of the moon, and their echo today between Sefardim and Ashkenazim and in which aliyah is most honored, shlishi or shishi. He brings the Midrash that the Yam Suf claimed seniority over Moshe, and explains that when Jews are in trouble there is no room for such quibbles.

title.en: The moon catches up in a leap year

summary.en: The Rav brings the haftarah's promise that the plowman will meet the reaper, which the Midrash reads as Yosef meeting Yehuda. He asks why in a leap year no sedras are combined during Sefirah and answers that the extra month lets the moon catch up with the sun, healing the diminishing of the moon, which is why the month is called Adar Sheni.

title.en: Iyar and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai unite all Jews

summary.en: The Rav explains that Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai binds all Jews together, so that at Meron, as at the Kosel, one sees every kind of Jew, and that Iyar is the bond between Hashem and Klal Yisrael. He returns to his opening question: Kedoshim, with v'ahavta l'rei'acha kamocha, unites all Jews and so was said to all of them together, and he ties Pesach Sheni and the mourning for Rabbi Akiva's students to the same theme.

catalogTitle: הדרכה לקיץ לבחורים הנוסעים להרים: עבודת ימי תמוז ואב להביא משיח ע"י חיזוק בהתמדת התורה' הכנה לשבת' טובת עין' עבודת התפילה

oneLiner.en: The Rav teaches that the forty days from Tammuz to Tisha b'Av, the days of the meraglim's mission, hide a blessing and the spark of Moshiach, to be drawn out through hasmadah in Torah, preparation for Shabbos, a generous eye toward others' honor, and davening with kavanah.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the meraglim, who went on their mission from the end of Tammuz until Tisha b'Av, and says these forty days are every year days of shlichus in which the meraglim's sin must be repaired. Through Balak, whose curse hid the root of Moshiach, he shows that the Three Weeks hide a blessing. The verse 'the days of the first grapes' hints that these days are under the power of evil, yet fruit can also ripen in them. Moshiach comes through Torah, so the bnei Torah must strengthen their hasmadah and use their time here to learn. He stresses the value of time, then preparation for Shabbos and for Shabbos davening. The meraglim's sin grew from jealousy over position, so the repair is to rejoice in another's honor, like Aharon. Kalev's tefillah leads to a discussion of davening aloud: its sources, its purpose of arousing kavanah, and its limits.

en: The forty days from Tammuz to Tisha b'Av are every year days of shlichus, in which one must repair what the meraglim spoiled.
Like Balak, whose curse hid the root of Moshiach, the Three Weeks look like days of curse but hold a blessing within.
Moshiach comes through Torah, so the bnei Torah, who carry the mesorah, must strengthen themselves in hasmadah.
Erev Shabbos is already a part of Shabbos, and one must prepare for Shabbos and for Shabbos davening rather than fall into it unprepared.
The meraglim's sin came from fear of losing their positions; its repair is to be content with another's honor.
Davening aloud is meant to arouse kavanah; it should be done with dignity and without strange noises or movements.

title.en: The meraglim's forty days and Balak's hidden blessing

summary.en: The Rav explains that the meraglim's mission, from the end of Tammuz to Tisha b'Av, makes these forty days a time of shlichus every year. He then shows through Balak, from whom Ruth and David descended, that the curse of the Three Weeks hides the blessing of Moshiach.

title.en: The days of the first grapes

summary.en: The Rav says one must not despair in these days but seek their blessing. He reads the verse 'the days of the first grapes' as a hint that these days are under the power of evil, which is why the meraglim fell, yet they are also days when fruit ripens and good can be brought out.

title.en: Moshiach comes through hasmadah in Torah

summary.en: The Rav brings the Or HaChaim that Moshiach will not come to those who neglect Torah, and explains that what is expected is not that all Jews learn, but that the bnei Torah not be idle. He reminds the listeners that they came here on a shlichus to bring Moshiach, and that the place and its clean air are suited for learning with hasmadah.

title.en: The blessing that remained, and the value of time

summary.en: The Rav notes that of Bilaam's blessings only the one on batei knesses and batei midrash remained. He then shows from the Rambam on kiddush hachodesh how central time is to Klal Yisrael, and says Torah and mitzvos in their proper time are worth far more.

title.en: Shabbos and erev Shabbos

summary.en: The Rav explains that Shabbos lets the neshama, torn from its source, reconnect, and that erev Shabbos is already a part of Shabbos, so it must not be wasted. He tells of a tzaddik who chose a match from a simple family because he saw how their home was ready for Shabbos by midday on Friday.

title.en: Preparing for Shabbos davening

summary.en: The Rav explains that Chassidim davened later on Shabbos in order to prepare, not to sleep longer, and describes being ready, after mikveh and brachos, by the time of davening. He asks for moderation at the Friday-night meal so one can daven in the morning, and tells of Rabbi Aharon of Karlin, who said the true pleasure is the soul's pleasure.

title.en: The meraglim's sin: jealousy over position

summary.en: The Rav brings the Zohar that the meraglim, who were leaders, feared they would be replaced in Eretz Yisrael, and their personal interest made them speak badly of the land. He applies this to the honors in a group, such as aliyos, and says the repair is to know that such thoughts are worthless and to be content with another's honor.

title.en: The danger of the top, and Aharon's good eye

summary.en: The Rav says it is best not to put oneself at the top, since what is on top is more easily disqualified, and that every small position brings great tests. He brings that Aharon merited to carry the choshen on his heart because he rejoiced in his heart over his younger brother Moshe's greatness.

title.en: Kalev's tefillah and the custom of davening aloud

summary.en: The Rav brings Rashi that Kalev went alone to Chevron to pray at the graves of the Avos to be saved from the meraglim's counsel, and says these forty days call for special tefillah. Asked about loud davening, he traces the custom to the talmidim of the Ba'al Shem Tov, including Rabbi Aharon of Karlin, and to the Ba'al HaTanya's writings.

title.en: The halachic basis: a loud voice arouses kavanah

summary.en: The Rav says that in halacha all the talmidim of the Ba'al Shem Tov follow the Ba'al HaTanya. He brings the Gemara on answering amen yehei shmei rabbah 'with all one's strength', the two readings of it, and the Shulchan Aruch with the Acharonim, who explain that a loud voice arouses kavanah, as with the first verse of Krias Shema. He points to Ne'ilah, when everyone davens aloud.

title.en: Every Maariv is Kol Nidrei, but without strange noises

summary.en: The Rav tells of two Kotzker Chassidim and the Kotzker Rebbe's words that by them every supper is a seder and every Maariv is Kol Nidrei, so one need not wait for Ne'ilah to daven with kavanah. Following Rabbeinu Yonah he says the parts of praise are said aloud, but warns against squealing and strange movements that invite mockery.

title.en: Levels of davening, and the closing blessing

summary.en: The Rav says those who daven better aloud should do so with fire but with order, and brings the Ruzhiner that the higher one is, the more the fire burns inside unseen. He describes levels from a loud voice to no visible motion at all, and closes with the wish that the curse of these days turn to blessing and the shlichus be fulfilled.

catalogTitle: נביא: דרוש בענין: אליהו הנביא בהר הכרמל - נשמה של לע"ל שיתקן כל יהודי

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains Eliyahu HaNavi's offering on Har HaCarmel as the descent of a soul from the world of tikkun to lift up Jews who are outside the camp, so that in the end Yerushalayim will reach as far as Damascus and every Jew, even a Gechazi, will reach his tikkun.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with Eliyahu's offering on Har HaCarmel at a time when sacrifices outside the Beis HaMikdash were forbidden, and with Rabbi Yochanan's statement that Eliyahu will expound the passage of neveilah and treifah. He lays down that a tzaddik must sometimes descend to lift the fallen, and applies it to Gechazi, whom the Mishnah excludes from the World to Come but the dorshei reshumos include. Through Pri Tzaddik he shows that a metzora cannot enter Yerushalayim, the camp of Israel, while Damascus is the seat of Naaman's lasting tzaraas. Eliyahu, a soul above sin, already stood in the future Yerushalayim, which will spread to Damascus, so the outcasts will be found inside it. He adds gematrios, the spelling Darmesek in Divrei HaYamim, and the role of Eliyahu in answering every kushya. He closes with Elul as Eliyahu's month, the low state of our generation and the great worth of its small avodah.

en: A tzaddik sometimes has to come down from his level, even to a trace of the sin itself, in order to lift up those who have fallen.
By offering outside on Har HaCarmel, Eliyahu reached the Jews who stood outside the camp of Israel and brought them to cry out that Hashem is G-d.
When Moshiach comes Yerushalayim will spread as far as Damascus, so that even those who cannot enter Yerushalayim, like Gechazi, will find themselves inside it.
Eliyahu will answer every kushya, because each difficulty in the Torah reflects a kushya on some Jew, and answering it brings that Jew back.
Elul is Eliyahu's month, the month of Gad, when the building of Yerushalayim begins and a time of tikkun for every soul.
Our generation has been thrown down into 'Damascus', and its small avodah is more precious to Hashem than the great avodah of earlier generations.

the generation of the footsteps of Moshiach

title.en: Eliyahu's offering outside on Har HaCarmel

summary.en: The Rav opens with Eliyahu offering a korban on Har HaCarmel when sacrifices outside the Beis HaMikdash were forbidden, and asks why he then needed atonement and exile. He brings the passuk in Yechezkel that the kohanim may not eat neveilah and treifah, and Rabbi Yochanan's statement that Eliyahu will expound it.

title.en: A tzaddik descends to lift the fallen

summary.en: The Rav asks why specifically Eliyahu will expound this passage, recalling that 'teiku' means Eliyahu will answer all questions. He lays down the principle that a tzaddik must sometimes fall from his level, with the parable of one on a roof who must climb down to lift something from the ground.

title.en: Moshe, Gechazi and the camp of Israel

summary.en: The Rav applies the principle to Moshe Rabbeinu and the egel, then turns to Gechazi, whom the Mishnah excludes from the World to Come, and to the Gemara that Elisha went to Damascus to bring him back. Through the Pri Tzaddik he explains that Gechazi's lasting tzaraas keeps him out of Yerushalayim, the camp of Israel, and so out of the World to Come.

title.en: Eliyahu lifts those outside the camp

summary.en: The Rav contrasts the Mishnah with the dorshei reshumos, who give Gechazi a share in the World to Come, and speaks of Jews who are driven outside the camp. Comparing them to a korban slaughtered outside the azarah, he explains that Eliyahu offered outside to lift such souls, and therefore needed atonement and went into exile toward Damascus.

title.en: Eliyahu, a soul above sin and time

summary.en: The Rav offers a second approach: Eliyahu never transgressed, since his soul has no connection to sin and belongs to the world of tikkun. He brings the Gemara where Eliyahu answered Rabbah bar Avuha in a cemetery of goyim, the Targum Yonasan that Pinchas is Eliyahu, and the teaching that in the days of Moshiach the halachah will follow Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the soul of Shabbos.

title.en: Yerushalayim and Damascus as opposites

summary.en: The Rav brings the Midrash that in the future Yerushalayim will reach Damascus, so Har HaCarmel will be within Yerushalayim and from Eliyahu's standpoint his offering was not outside. He explains that Yerushalayim and Damascus are opposites: Damascus is the seat of Naaman's lasting tzaraas, which drew Gechazi there, and tzaraas comes from lashon hara and machlokes.

title.en: When Yerushalayim reaches Damascus

summary.en: The Rav explains that when Yerushalayim spreads to Damascus the outcasts will find themselves inside it. He brings the Yalkut that the Beis HaMikdash will stand on Har HaCarmel among other mountains, gematrios linking Eretz HaCarmel to Yerushalayim and Boneh Yerushalayim Hashem to Aram Damesek, and explains Eliyahu's flight to Damascus and his anointing of Chazael as showing his mastery over Damascus.

title.en: Darmesek in Divrei HaYamim

summary.en: The Rav notes that Divrei HaYamim always spells Damascus 'Darmesek' with a reish. He explains that the twenty-four books of Tanach parallel the twenty-four adornments of the bride and the combinations of Hashem's Name of malchus, that Divrei HaYamim is the last book which completes malchus and leans toward the world of tikkun, and that Darmesek equals machaneh Yisrael; with Eliyahu's power Elisha went there to repair Gechazi.

title.en: Eliyahu, Elisha and Gechazi; answering every kushya

summary.en: The Rav brings the Chiddushei HaRim that the highest gilui Eliyahu is when Eliyahu comes with Elisha and Gechazi runs after them. He explains that every Jew is a letter in the Torah, so a kushya in the Torah reflects a kushya on some Jew, and toiling to answer it brings that Jew to teshuvah; this is Eliyahu's task of 'teiku' and of turning the hearts of fathers to sons.

title.en: Why only Eliyahu can explain neveilah and treifah

summary.en: The Rav returns to the opening question: the passuk of neveilah and treifah remains difficult because souls rooted in it belong to the klipos and have no tikkun until the future, so only Eliyahu can expound it. He adds that Eliyahu is the angel of the bris, tied to the circumcision of the heart hinted in the word Elul.

title.en: Elul, the month of Gad and of Eliyahu

summary.en: The Rav explains that Eliyahu comes from the tribe of Gad and Elul is Gad's month, when the building of Yerushalayim and of malchus begins, from Tisha B'Av through the reading of Sefer Devarim. He tells how a grandson of Rabbi Yitzchak of Skver ran to see Eliyahu and instead came to a right thought about parnassah, and says that whoever spends Elul properly receives Eliyahu by Erev Rosh Hashanah.

title.en: Our generation thrown into Damascus

summary.en: The Rav describes the footsteps of Moshiach as the lowest generation, with trials of a kind earlier generations never faced, and says we have been thrown into Damascus. He explains that we must repair what the great souls could not reach, and that Hashem watches over us like a babysitter, present even in the lowest depths.

title.en: The worth of small avodah

summary.en: The Rav teaches that the small avodah of our generation is more precious than the great avodah of earlier ones: a Jew who does not look in the street gives up his will, which is mesiras nefesh. He brings the Maggid of Mezritch's parable of the king who delights in a talking bird, and the Sidduro shel Shabbos parable of the servant who brought a simple pearl from the depths of the sea, which the king placed at the head of his crown.

title.en: Every Gechazi will reach his tikkun

summary.en: The Rav says we are all Gechazis in the time of Damascus, but Elul, the time of Eliyahu and of good thoughts, is coming, when Jews learn Tikkunei Zohar. He concludes that when Moshiach comes Eliyahu will come with Elisha and Gechazi, prays on the Shabbos of blessing the month of Elul that Yerushalayim reach our Damascus, and blesses that each one work on his own Gechazi.

catalogTitle: יארצייט: יארצייט של ר' שרגא פייוול מענדלאוויץ זצ”ל (ג' אלול)

oneLiner.en: On the yahrtzeit of Reb Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz, the Rav describes him as an eved Hashem whose whole life was a Shabbos niggun of shleimus and harmony, a song that still sings in the yeshiva.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the end of the Torah: Moshe is called both 'ish ha'Elokim' and 'eved Hashem', and Yehoshua, who wrote the last pesukim, could describe him only from his own level, as eved Hashem. Like a blade of grass that also benefits from the sun, the Rav will describe Reb Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz as an eved Hashem: a builder of Torah in America who sat in the last bench and refused titles. His deepest teacher was his own neshamah, a neshamah of Shabbos, which is shleimus, and of shirah, which is harmony, like seven notes making one melody. The Rav brings the 'seventh' in creation, Eretz Yisrael as a land of song, and stories of a torn leaf whose song was interrupted. Every life is a niggun; his was a Shabbos niggun, seen in his love of creation's beauty, the flowers he planted, the harmony he made between groups, the best talmidim he gave away, and his kabbalos. His niggun still sings.

en: Yehoshua could describe Moshe only as 'eved Hashem', from his own level; likewise the Rav describes Reb Shraga Feivel as an eved Hashem.
Reb Shraga Feivel built Torah in America yet wanted no honor or title, preferring to remain a plain Jew.
His main teacher was his own neshamah, a neshamah of Shabbos and of shirah: Shabbos is shleimus, and shirah is harmony.
Every part of creation sings shirah to Hashem, and every person's life is a niggun; his life was one long Shabbos niggun.
As an eved Hashem he sent his best talmidim to build other yeshivos, and his niggun still sings in the yeshiva.

title.en: Moshe: ish ha'Elokim and eved Hashem

summary.en: The Rav opens with the last parsha of the Torah, where Moshe is called 'ish ha'Elokim', and explains that Yehoshua, who wrote the last pesukim, could describe him only as 'eved Hashem'. Comparing himself to a blade of grass that also benefits from the sun, he says he too will try to describe Reb Shraga Feivel.

title.en: A builder of Torah who sat in the last bench

summary.en: The Rav describes Reb Shraga Feivel as an eved Hashem: he planted Torah in America, yet sought no honor, sat in the last bench at the dedication of the new building he had organized, and taught his talmidim Tanya and Shaarei Teshuvah. He did not take a title and preferred to remain a plain Jew.

title.en: A neshamah of Shabbos and of shirah

summary.en: The Rav says Reb Shraga Feivel's main rebbe was his own neshamah, a Shabbos neshamah: on Erev Shabbos he became a different person. Shabbos is shleimus, and shirah is harmony, like seven notes; he brings the 'seventh' in creation and Eretz Yisrael as a land of song, and concludes that Reb Shraga Feivel was not limited to one area but was a neshamah of shleimus.

title.en: The leaf that sings

summary.en: The Rav tells how in camp Reb Shraga Feivel stopped a talmid who tore off a leaf, since he had interrupted its shirah, and how in Monsey he saw one leaf moving among still ones as the chazan. He adds that Reb Shraga Feivel would repeat that every person's life is a niggun sung to Hashem.

title.en: Beauty of creation and harmony between groups

summary.en: The Rav explains that Reb Shraga Feivel taught bochurim to develop a sense for the beauty of creation in order to thank Hashem, bringing David Hamelech and the Rambam. In Monsey he planted flowers among the first things, and in the yeshiva he made a harmony between Hungarian Jews, Litvish roshei yeshiva and chassidus.

title.en: Giving away his best talmidim

summary.en: The Rav relates that Reb Shraga Feivel sent his best talmidim to found other yeshivos, and he tells the bochurim to remember, when they are in business, what it means to give one's best people to a competitor. He did this because he was an eved Hashem.

title.en: A path for each bochur; the niggun still sings

summary.en: The Rav says Reb Shraga Feivel had no single method but a separate path for each bochur, and tells of kabbalos found after his passing: to find a new idea every day to improve the yeshiva and to love every bochur. He concludes that his spirit remains in the yeshiva and his niggun is still sung.

catalogTitle: רשב”י - The נשמה of משיח

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai is the aspect of Mashiach and of Yovel, the great return, who abolishes mourning, heals the jealousy that destroyed the Beis HaMikdash, unites all Jews, and on Lag Ba'omer gives a real tikkun beyond Pesach Sheni.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the concept of Yovel, introduced in this week's sedra: Yovel means return, and its shofar, like the shofar of Ne'ilah and of Mashiach, brings every Jew back to his root. Even the eved nirtza, whom Shemitah cannot free, goes out at Yovel. Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai's mitzvah is Yovel; he is the aspect of Mashiach. Through the Rambam's signs of Mashiach and the end of mourning, the Rav explains why Lag Ba'omer is pure joy, with stories from Meron. Rabbi Akiva's students died for lack of mutual respect, the jealousy rooted in the moon's complaint; Mashiach will repair it, and Rashbi, who can redeem even the lowest, unites all Jews as the Beis HaMikdash did. A mashal of the last tug teaches that each small mitzvah may complete the building. This year is special for geulah. Finally, Pesach Sheni gives a partial tikkun, while Lag Ba'omer, like Purim, looks forward to the Pesach of Mashiach.

en: Yovel means return: its shofar, like the shofar of Ne'ilah and the shofar of Mashiach, brings every Jew back to his root.
Every Jew has a mitzvah that is his root, and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai's mitzvah is Yovel; he is the aspect of Mashiach.
Mashiach abolishes mourning, and so the day of Rashbi's passing is a day of joy rather than mourning.
Rabbi Akiva's students died because they did not show each other respect, a jealousy rooted in the flaw of the moon, which Mashiach will repair.
The Beis HaMikdash was the place of unity and was destroyed by baseless hatred; Rashbi, who unites all Jews, is like the Beis HaMikdash.
Pesach Sheni, chesed shebehod, is only a substitute tikkun, while Lag Ba'omer, hod shebehod, gives a real tikkun, a Pesach of the future.

title.en: Yovel, the great return

summary.en: The Rav introduces Yovel from this week's sedra: it means return, its shofar is like the shofar of Ne'ilah and of Mashiach, and it frees even the eved nirtza whom Shemitah cannot free. He concludes that Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai's mitzvah is Yovel and that he is the aspect of Mashiach.

title.en: Mashiach returns Jews and ends mourning

summary.en: The Rav brings the Rambam's sign of one who is presumed to be Mashiach, explaining it as bringing Jews back to their roots. He then explains that Mashiach abolishes mourning, and that on the day of Rashbi's passing one does not fast but rejoices.

title.en: No mourning in Meron; Rabbi Akiva's students

summary.en: The Rav tells of a great Rebbe who had people dance in Meron on the fifth of Av, and Rabbi Chaim Vital's account of a man punished for saying Nachem at Rashbi's celebration. He then explains that Rashbi annulled the mourning for Rabbi Akiva's students, who died for not showing each other respect.

title.en: Jealousy, the flaw of the moon

summary.en: The Rav traces jealousy to the moon's complaint against the sun and follows it through the snake, Kayin, Yosef's brothers and the kings of Israel. He notes there is no English word for being happy at another's success, and says Mashiach will repair the flaw of the moon.

title.en: Rashbi strengthens even the lowest

summary.en: The Rav brings a well-known saying that Rashbi gives strength even to the lowest, and the Gemara that Rashbi can exempt the whole world from judgment. He connects the end of jealousy between Ephraim and Yehudah with the baseless hatred that destroyed the Beis HaMikdash, which the Maharal calls the place of unity.

title.en: Coming to Rashbi is like coming to Yerushalayim

summary.en: The Rav brings the Zohar that Rashbi is the 'face of the Master, Hashem', so coming to him is like coming to the Beis HaMikdash, and in Meron every kind of Jew gathers. Yovel applies only when all Jews are together in the land, and Rashbi, who unites all Jews, is in the aspect of Yovel, which appears now in Behar and Bechukosai.

title.en: Kamtza and Bar Kamtza: the last tug

summary.en: The Rav asks why the Gemara tells the story of Kamtza and Bar Kamtza and brings a great tzaddik's mashal of strong men who loosened a tree that a child then pulled down. Kamtza and Bar Kamtza were the last tug after generations of hatred, and in the same way the last generation will give the last small tug to build the Beis HaMikdash.

title.en: A year auspicious for geulah

summary.en: The Rav explains that a year in which Shabbos falls within Pesach is auspicious for geulah, and that this year Lag Ba'omer falls on Friday and carries into Shabbos, making it a stronger Lag Ba'omer. He warns against meddling in speculation about Mashiach: the task is to learn, daven, do chesed and do mitzvos.

title.en: Pesach Sheni and the tumah of tzaddikim

summary.en: After a Zohar on the whispered command in Emor, the Rav brings the Zohar that Pesach Sheni is only a substitute for those who missed the first Pesach. He asks how that fits the Gemara that they were tzaddikim, and brings the Yismach Moshe: the graves of tzaddikim do not defile, but the Torah could not write so since no one knows who is a tzaddik; only Moshe Rabbeinu, who could ask Hashem, could decide.

title.en: From Pesach Sheni to Lag Ba'omer, and Purim

summary.en: The Rav compares the Bnos Tzelofchad and explains that those who asked were really permitted, while Pesach Sheni was given for later generations. Pesach Sheni, chesed shebehod, is a partial tikkun, but Lag Ba'omer, hod shebehod, gives a real Pesach. Through the At-Bash calendar rule he shows that Purim looks forward to the Pesach of Mashiach, and Lag Ba'omer falls on Purim's weekday.

title.en: Nefesh, ruach, neshamah: two promises of Yovel

summary.en: The Rav brings the Ba'al Shem Tov that a flaw in deed, speech or thought shows in one's property, wife or children. Yovel promises two returns, to one's property and to one's family; Pesach Sheni brings only the lower return of property, while Lag Ba'omer brings the higher one.

catalogTitle: הכנסת כלה: א מצוה באזונדער מסוגל אויף ביאת המשיח (ביאור ענין יחוד קוב"ה ושכינתיה' עניניא דיומא - ערד ציטערניש בהייטי)

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that hachnasas kallah stands out among the mitzvos as a source of rescue and of bringing the geulah, because the aim of every mitzvah is the union of Hashem, the Chassan, with Klal Yisrael, the Kallah.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the teaching of Rabbi Dovid of Lelov that hachnasas kallah, placed in the list of birchos hashachar between visiting the sick and what comes after, saves a person from what follows it, and says one should give for it knowing it is a great rescue. He turns to the unsettled times and the earthquake in Haiti, citing the passuk in Tehillim that Hashem looks at the earth and it trembles, and tells how the Chofetz Chaim gathered his town in Radin to speak about a flood on the Mississippi. He explains the reason from Rashi in Parshas Va'eira: Hashem brings punishment on the nations so that the Jews take mussar, and he calls for strengthening in every area. Then he explains 'leshem yichud': every mitzvah aims at uniting the Chassan and the Kallah, so hachnasas kallah itself arouses Heaven most, and he closes with a brachah for the geulah.

en: Following Rabbi Dovid of Lelov, hachnasas kallah stands between visiting the sick and what follows it because it rescues a person from what comes after.
A disaster among the nations, like the earthquake in Haiti, is meant for the Jews, as Rashi says that Hashem punishes the nations so that the Jews will fear and take mussar.
The Rav says Jews must take this to heart and strengthen themselves in every area, including the chinuch of children and tznius in dress.
Every mitzvah is said 'leshem yichud', for the union of Hashem, the Chassan of Shir Hashirim, with Klal Yisrael, His Kallah, who are now apart in galus.
Since the aim of every mitzvah is a kind of hachnasas kallah, the actual mitzvah of hachnasas kallah arouses Heaven more than any other.

candidateTopics: Hashem and Klal Yisrael as chassan and kallah

title.en: Hachnasas kallah rescues from what follows

summary.en: The Rav speaks of the great nachas in Heaven from helping Jews marry off their children, and brings Rabbi Dovid of Lelov's teaching that hachnasas kallah, placed in birchos hashachar between visiting the sick and what follows, saves from what comes after. He says that had he known this, he would have given far more, and that one should give knowing it is a great rescue from harsh decrees.

title.en: The Haiti earthquake and the Chofetz Chaim

summary.en: The Rav describes the unsettled times and the earthquake in Haiti, brings the passuk in Tehillim that Hashem looks at the earth and it trembles, and asks what it has to do with Jews. He tells how the Chofetz Chaim gathered the whole town of Radin for a drasha about a flood on the Mississippi, so that people should not ignore it.

title.en: Rashi in Va'eira: punishment of nations is for the Jews

summary.en: The Rav notes that the earthquake came in the week of Parshas Va'eira, where Rashi brings the passuk in Tzefaniah that Hashem destroys nations so that the Jews will fear and take mussar. He explains that the disaster is a message to Jews everywhere, that great plans for geulah are being prepared in Heaven, and that Jews must strengthen themselves in every area.

title.en: Leshem yichud: the Chassan and the Kallah

summary.en: The Rav asks why hachnasas kallah, of all mitzvos, is the one placed as the interruption. He explains 'leshem yichud' said before every mitzvah: Hashem and Klal Yisrael are Chassan and Kallah as in Shir Hashirim, separated in galus, and every mitzvah aims at their union in the geulah.

title.en: Collectors during davening; the women's resolution

summary.en: The Rav addresses complaints about collectors for hachnasas kallah going around during davening and says he thanks such a person, because he reminds him that his davening is meant to be hachnasas kallah. He praises the women's resolution to work for hachnasas kallah, the mitzvah that arouses Heaven most, and closes with a brachah for the geulah.

catalogTitle: סעודת הודאה: סעודת הודאה - ר"ח ניסן (ור' מרדכי פינקלמאן)

oneLiner.en: At a seudas hodaah on the eve of Rosh Chodesh Nissan, the Rav explains that a Jew must praise Hashem with his life and with every extra year he is given, and that the days of the nesiim are days of chinuch, of starting anew.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the passuk 'I will praise Hashem with my life' and brings the Kedushas Levi: everything was created for Hashem's honor, even the rasha, whose 'song' is his downfall, while the tzaddik praises Hashem with his life. He tells of two times the Gerrer Rebbe, for whom every minute counted, was 'defeated': by a man struggling twenty years with a sick daughter, and by a blind chassid who did not want 'gifted years' without learning. From this he reads 'with my extra being' as praising Hashem with the extra years. After a story of a chassid of the Ba'al HaTanya, he says every Jew must contemplate his tafkid. The twelve days of the nesiim, whose korbanos defeat the nesiim of Yishmael, are days of chinuch, of starting anew; he closes with a brachah for the Beis HaMikdash.

en: According to the Rav, a Jew must praise the Ribono shel Olam with his life itself, as the passuk says 'I will praise Hashem with my life'.
Everything, even the rasha, was created for Hashem's honor; the rasha brings it out through his downfall, the tzaddik through his life.
The extra years a person is given are meant to be used to sing to Hashem, not merely to be lived through.
Every Jew came into the world for a particular tafkid, and should contemplate what it is.
The twelve days of the nesiim are days of chinuch, in which one leaves the old behind and begins anew.

summary.en: The Rav brings the Kedushas Levi on 'I will praise Hashem with my life': the rasha glorifies Hashem through his downfall, the tzaddik with his life. He tells of the two times the Gerrer Rebbe was 'defeated', the second by a blind chassid who did not want 'gifted years', and reads 'with my extra being' as singing to Hashem with the extra years.

title.en: Every Jew's tafkid; the days of the nesiim

summary.en: After a story of a chassid who asked the Ba'al HaTanya for years he could accomplish something with, the Rav says each person must contemplate his tafkid. He explains that the twelve days of the nesiim, beginning that night, defeat the nesiim of Yishmael and are days of chinuch for renewing oneself, and closes with a brachah for the third Beis HaMikdash.

title.en: R' Mordechai Finkelman's words of thanks

summary.en: R' Mordechai Finkelman is called up and speaks about the seudas hodaah for the Rav's recovery, which each participant feels is his own, and tells how the Rav once advised him as a young man to return to camp rather than start a career.

title.en: R' Finkelman on mesiras nefesh in Shema

summary.en: R' Finkelman repeats ideas he heard on the mesiras nefesh of Shema Yisrael, ending with the thought that living with mesiras nefesh is greater than dying for Hashem, and that a person should see himself as a korban.

title.en: R' Finkelman's application and wishes

summary.en: R' Finkelman applies the idea to the kehillah: fixed times for learning, davening together and caring for one another, and closes with wishes for the Rav's health and for the geulah.

catalogTitle: חיזוק: נועם שירת דור הצפרדע

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains why the frog's song in Perek Shirah is 'Baruch shem kevod malchuso', and that the lowly generation of the footsteps of Moshiach is a generation of frogs whose song is especially dear to Hashem.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the reversal between land and sea: species impure on land are pure in the sea, and the reverse. He then brings the opening of Perek Shirah, where the frog tells King David that its song is finer than his, and the dispute of Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah over 'the frog' in the singular. Through the Bnei Yissaschar and the Avnei Nezer he links the plague to the Egyptians' attempt to mix good with evil. He explains that every species sings through a pure counterpart that acts as its shliach tzibbur, but the frog lives on land and in the sea and has none, so its song is 'Baruch shem', the hidden praise of Hashem's presence even in impure places, said quietly. Tumah begins with 'two', which resolves the Midrash. He then applies this to our generation, the heel of Moshiach: a generation of frogs, facing new trials, whose weak service with mesiras nefesh is precious to Hashem, strengthened by Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and the week of hod, and he closes with the three 'remember's.

en: Every species sings to Hashem through its pure counterpart, but the frog, which belongs to both land and sea, has none, so its song in Perek Shirah is 'Baruch shem kevod malchuso'.
'Baruch shem' is the lower unity: Hashem watches over and sustains even the lowliest and impure places, a praise that is not fitting to proclaim aloud and is therefore said quietly.
The Rav says our generation is the heel of Moshiach, facing new kinds of yetzer hara that never existed before, so it cannot hold on without mesiras nefesh.
Our generation is a generation of frogs, and its weak service in a time of hidden face is more precious to Hashem than the service of earlier generations.
The power of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, connected to hod, strengthens even the lowest souls in every generation.
The Rav closes with the Torah's 'remember's: remember Amalek, because there is a great yetzer hara, and remember Miriam, so as not to spoil the frog's song with lashon hara and machlokes.

candidateTopics: purity of land and sea creatures
Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and hod

title.en: Impure on land, pure in the sea

summary.en: After opening words and the verse of the stragglers attacked by Amalek, the Rav brings the Ba'al HaTurim and the Gemara that the sea-donkey is pure and the sea-ox impure, and asks why Hashem reversed land and sea. He notes Tosafos limits this to those two animals, while the Divrei Yoel holds it is a general rule.

title.en: The frog and King David; one frog or many

summary.en: The Rav brings the opening of Perek Shirah, where a frog tells King David not to be proud because its song is finer than his, and wonders at it, since the frog's voice is the least pleasant. He then brings the Midrash on 'the frog' in the singular: Rabbi Akiva says one frog swarmed into multitudes, and Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah rebukes him and says one frog whistled and the rest came.

title.en: The frog plague from yesod; mixing good and evil

summary.en: The Rav brings the Bnei Yissaschar that the plague of frogs came from yesod, since the plagues went from below upward, and connects it to Pharaoh's plan to kill the males and take the females. Adding the Avnei Nezer that a mixture of good and evil is worse for Jews than evil itself, he explains the Egyptians wanted to create such a mixture.

title.en: The pure counterpart as shliach tzibbur

summary.en: The Rav explains that song must come in holiness and purity, so Hashem made each species pure in one realm and impure in the other; the pure one sings as shliach tzibbur for its impure counterpart. The frog lives in both the sea and on land, so no pure counterpart can sing for it; it is itself a mixture of tamei and tahor, fitting punishment for the Egyptians' mixture.

title.en: Baruch shem said quietly: the lower unity

summary.en: The Rav brings the Gemara in Pesachim that Yaakov's sons said Shema and Yaakov answered 'Baruch shem', which is said quietly like a princess craving the scrapings of the pot. Citing the Tanya's Shaar HaYichud and other sefarim, he explains Shema as the higher unity and Baruch shem as the lower unity, Hashem's providence even over impure places, which is not honorable to say aloud. He contrasts the sitra achra, which acknowledges Hashem but is not batel, like Bilam, with Avraham, who nullified his will at the Akeidah.

title.en: Why the frog's song is Baruch shem

summary.en: The Rav asks why, in Perek Shirah, the frog alone says no verse but 'Baruch shem kevod malchuso'. Having no pure shliach tzibbur, it may not say a verse, yet no creature's song may be missing, so it sings the lower unity quietly. He supports this with a Midrash that when a Jew says Shema the mazikin whisper 'Baruch shem', so they too have a right to exist.

title.en: Tumah begins with 'two'

summary.en: The Rav brings the Rambam's explanation of the order of Seder Taharos, where Ohalos and then Negaim deal with the gravest tumah, and notes that both begin with the word 'two'. Twoness is the opposite of oneness: Gehinom and machlokes were created on the second day, and the same appears in the laws of carrying on Shabbos and false oaths.

title.en: Resolving Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah

summary.en: Returning to the Midrash, the Rav explains that Rabbi Akiva's single frog as the root of the plague cannot be, since impurity cannot stem from oneness, and Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah points to Negaim and Ohalos, which begin with 'two'. Yet the frog is a mixture, so the plague had both one and many: one frog whistled and the others came. The whistle, shuruk, is the vowel of yesod.

title.en: The heel of Moshiach and its new trials

summary.en: The Rav says tzaddikim before the war foresaw that we are at the heel of Moshiach: the generations are like a body from head to heel, and ours is the lowest. Alongside many who learn and daven, new kinds of yetzer hara, such as the electronic one, are trapping even the finest, because the yetzer hara knows its end is near. He brings the Arizal's words to Rabbi Chaim Vital about a lowly generation, and calls ours a generation of the frog.

title.en: The frogs' mesiras nefesh and our song

summary.en: The Rav brings that Chananyah, Mishael and Azaryah learned mesiras nefesh from the frogs that jumped into the ovens, and says that today the whole world is a burning furnace and one cannot hold on without mesiras nefesh. Like the princess who preferred the scrapings of the pot, Hashem prefers the service of today's generation; the frog of Perek Shirah is today's Jew telling David's generation that its song is finer. Even a davening full of foreign thoughts is precious, because it is service in a time of hidden face.

title.en: Hod, the heel, and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai

summary.en: The Rav compares our generation to the heel, which stays dark even under the summer sun, and to hod, the lowest sefirah and the left leg, as in Pesach Eliyahu. Citing the Beis Aharon, he says Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai gives strength to the lowest souls. Purim belongs to hod and to the stragglers whom Amalek attacks, the tribe of Dan according to Targum Yonasan, and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai is the gematria of hod.

title.en: The week of hod and 'Roni akarah'

summary.en: The Rav lays out the seven weeks from Pesach to Shavuos and from Tisha B'Av to Rosh Hashanah, and says the fifth week of consolation is the week of hod, when the parshah of Amalek is read. The haftarah 'Roni akarah' with 'for more are the children of the desolate' is explained by a Midrash: the righteous in exile are precious to Hashem, and the phrase is the gematria of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai. Remembering Amalek is a reminder that there is a great yetzer hara.

title.en: A great yetzer hara; remember Miriam

summary.en: The Rav tells of an elder who, days before his passing, would say only that a tzaddik had said there is a great yetzer hara. He then brings the remembrance of Miriam: one should not spoil the frog's song with lashon hara and machlokes, and the three 'remember's of Shabbos, Amalek and Miriam are three trials to beware of. He closes with a brachah for teshuvah and the redemption.

catalogTitle: The Light of יובל Begins to be Revealed

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that Yovel, the power of return, reaches even the lowest Jewish souls that Shabbos cannot help, and that its light begins to shine in the week of Hod and on Lag Ba'omer.

abstract.en: The Rav reviews how the soul, a part of G-d above, descends through many contractions, and how holy sparks fell into the klipos through the breaking of the vessels. Following the Tanya's parable of the body, he describes the souls of each generation from head to toenails: the attached part of the nail is the sinner still bound to Yiddishkeit, the protruding part is the heretic cut off before Shabbos. Shabbos and Shemitah free the Eved Ivri, who sold himself to the Sitra Achra, the 'maidservant that inherits her mistress'; but one who refuses Shabbos is released only by Yovel, the law of return. Shavuos, the fiftieth day, is a small Yovel, as shown by Rus who 'returned'. Pesach Sheni opens the week of Hod and Lag Ba'omer, Hod sheb'Hod, closes it: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, like the Beis HaMikdash, gathers all Jews, and this year Lag Ba'omer extends into Shabbos.

en: Every soul, even the lowest, remains bound to its source, as even the toenails draw from the brain in the Tanya's parable.
The attached part of the nail stands for sinners still bound to Yiddishkeit; the protruding part stands for heretics, cut off before Shabbos.
Shabbos and Shemitah free the Eved Ivri from the Sitra Achra, but one who clings to his servitude is freed only by Yovel.
Yovel is the law of return: every Jewish soul, even one discarded like a cut nail, will ultimately return with the shofar of Mashiach.
Pesach Sheni at the start of the week of Hod and Lag Ba'omer at its end are second chances, when the light of Yovel is already seen.
Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai is like the Beis HaMikdash and the Kohen Gadol: a place of unity, where there is no mourning and all Jews come together.

sparks of holiness and the breaking of the vessels

title.en: Contractions, broken vessels and holy sparks

summary.en: The Rav reviews that the soul is a part of G-d above that comes down through contractions, using the parable of pouring wine from a barrel into a bottle. He explains the breaking of the vessels, the sparks that fell into the klipos, and how a Jew frees them by using his food, clothing and home for the service of Hashem.

title.en: From the head to the toenails

summary.en: The Rav compares the soul's coverings to insulation on a wire and brings the Tanya's parable of the body, where even the toenails remain bound to the brain. He applies it to the souls of each generation and distinguishes two levels of nail: the attached part, sinners still bound to Yiddishkeit, and the protruding part, heretics, which is cut off before Shabbos.

title.en: The Eved Ivri and the maidservant

summary.en: The Rav explains that the Eved Ivri, permitted to a maidservant, has fallen into the Sitra Achra and lost his Jewish lineage. He brings the passuk in Mishlei about the maidservant who inherits her mistress and explains it as the power of evil dominating in exile, when the nations take the bounty first.

title.en: Yaakov and Esav, Yerushalayim and Rome

summary.en: The Rav describes the constant war between Yaakov and Esav, from the birth when Yaakov held Esav's heel, to the rivalry of Yerushalayim and Rome. He brings the Tzvi LaTzaddik that Yerushalayim is spelled without a yud in exile, and that Mashiach will add it; Shabbos frees the Eved Ivri from the maidservant's grip.

title.en: Yovel, the law of return, and Rus

summary.en: The Rav explains why nails are cut before Shabbos: they are the Jew so sunk in the Sitra Achra that he refuses Shabbos's rescue. Yet no Jew is lost forever; Yovel returns him to Klal Yisrael. Shavuos, the fiftieth day, is a small Yovel, which is why Rus, a Jewish soul born in Moav who 'returned', is read then; the shofar of Mashiach will bring back every soul.

title.en: The week of Hod and Pesach Sheni

summary.en: The Rav explains that the days of Sefirah prepare for the fiftieth day: five weeks refine the middos and the last two polish them, so the work is essentially done with Hod. The week of Hod opens with Pesach Sheni, a second chance for those who were impure, with the light of Yovel already visible; he brings the teaching about a convert and the Korban Pesach.

title.en: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and the Beis HaMikdash

summary.en: The Rav explains that Pesach and milah, the only positive mitzvos carrying kareis, bind a Jew to Hashem. Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai is the aspect of building the Beis HaMikdash, which stands for unity and was destroyed through baseless hatred; Yovel too requires all Jews together. Like the Kohen Gadol, who does not mourn, Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai has no mourning.

title.en: No mourning in Meron; Hod sheb'Hod

summary.en: The Rav brings Rav Chaim Vital's account of a disciple of the Arizal who said Nachem on Lag Ba'omer and was punished. He compares Meron to the Kosel, the two places that draw the whole spectrum of Jews, and explains Hod sheb'Hod as the lowest level, where holiness is strong enough to reach the very bottom.

title.en: The gates are open

summary.en: The Rav brings the Zohar that a heavenly crier announces the gates are open, and the Ba'al HaTanya that the Yom Kippur tekiah is the shofar of Yovel. He explains that a taste of Yovel reaches even the lowest Jews on Lag Ba'omer, who feel it tugging at their hearts, and says Hashem is now beckoning everyone to come in and take Torah, tefillah and closeness.

title.en: Lag Ba'omer on Friday stays for Shabbos

summary.en: The Rav calls this a special year, citing the Chasam Sofer, and notes that Lag Ba'omer falls on Friday. A Yom Tov on Friday stays into Shabbos, as Shabbos kept Adam HaRishon in Gan Eden according to Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer, so there are two days of Lag Ba'omer, two days of the great shofar of Yovel.

catalogTitle: חנוכת הבית ל'שטיבל' בביתר: מסירת נפש לתפילה וענין דיבוק חבירים (מספר שומר אמונים)

oneLiner.en: At the opening of a new beis medrash, the Rav teaches that in the days before Moshiach tefillah is the main avodah and demands constant mesiras nefesh, and that the foundation of the Ba'al Shem Tov's path is love between friends and among all Jews, as the sefer Shomer Emunim writes.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with thanks to those who built the new beis medrash and with the bracha 'matziv gevul almanah', explaining that Klal Yisroel is only 'like' a widow, since the Husband will return. Every new good thing draws the opposition of Amalek, and in the days before Moshiach nothing is achieved without mesiras nefesh. Tefillah, which Chazal call a thing standing at the height of the world yet treated lightly, is now the main avodah that will bring the geulah, so Amalek fights it most; one must ignore the scoffers and give up time and wishes daily, since many small sacrifices add up to more than one great one. He then explains the chassidic innovation of dibuk chaverim, citing the Divrei Chaim and the Ba'al Shem Tov, and reads at length from the Shomer Emunim on love of tzaddikim, friends and all Jews and on avoiding division. He explains that each shevet and each kehillah has its own nusach and ways from its own root above, that friends brought together share a root of the soul, and closes with brachos for the new beis medrash.

en: Every new good undertaking is attacked by Amalek, and in the days before Moshiach nothing can be achieved without mesiras nefesh.
In the days before Moshiach tefillah is the main avodah that will bring the geulah, though Torah study loses none of its greatness.
Constant mesiras nefesh is the great avodah: giving up any wish, such as a daily half hour to forty minutes for davening, is mesiras nefesh, and the small ones add up.
The Ba'al Shem Tov laid a great foundation on dibuk chaverim, and the Divrei Chaim explains that chassidic batei knesses are built on condition so that friends can eat and farbreng there.
Following the Shomer Emunim, love of tzaddikim, of friends and of all Jews is the heart of chassidus, and division between chassidic groups goes against the Ba'al Shem Tov's intent.
Each shevet has its own gate above and its own nusach and halachic ways, and people whom Providence brings together as friends share one root of the soul.

candidateTopics: tefillah in the days before Moshiach

title.en: Thanks and the bracha of the widow

summary.en: After a stretch of unusable audio, the Rav thanks those who worked with great dedication to build the beis medrash and brings the bracha 'matziv gevul almanah' said over a rebuilt beis haknesses. He explains that Klal Yisroel is only 'like' a widow, for the Husband will return.

title.en: Amalek attacks every new beginning

summary.en: The Rav says every good thing comes together with its opposite, and Amalek especially attacks the start of something new, so young men who begin a new undertaking must strengthen themselves against it. He cites a saying in the name of the Imrei Emes and of Belz that in the days before Moshiach nothing is reached without mesiras nefesh, and says the beis medrash is not built for a party but for avodas Hashem.

title.en: Tefillah as the main avodah before Moshiach

summary.en: The Rav brings the Gemara that tefillah stands at the height of the world yet people treat it lightly, and says that before Moshiach tefillah is the main avodah, illustrated by a sick man for whom orange juice matters more than bread. Amalek therefore fights tefillah most; one must ignore the scoffers and have constant mesiras nefesh, such as giving a half hour to forty minutes a day to davening.

title.en: Dibuk chaverim in the chassidic shtibel

summary.en: The Rav explains that a 'bayis gadol' is one where Torah and tefillah are made great, and that chassidus brought a new element to the beis haknesses: dibuk chaverim. He cites the Divrei Chaim that chassidic shuls are built on condition so friends can eat and farbreng there, the Ba'al Shem Tov's foundation of love between friends and the Arizal's practice before davening, and says that today, amid great breaches, the shtibel must be a place where friends give each other advice in Yiddishkeit.

title.en: Shomer Emunim on love of friends and all Jews

summary.en: The Rav reads from the sefer Shomer Emunim that what remains from the tzaddikim of old is love of tzaddikim, of friends and of all Jews, that Klal Yisroel as a whole has no blemish, and that division between chassidic groups is against the Ba'al Shem Tov's will. He then applies it: going to a friend's simcha, helping families when a wife gives birth, and dealing with a wrongdoer gently rather than with zealotry that comes from one's own anger.

title.en: Against division and lashon hara between groups

summary.en: The Rav continues reading the Shomer Emunim: through love of Jews one reaches the highest levels, the aim of the Ba'al Shem Tov's path is unity among Jews, and one must not speak lashon hara about any group of chassidim but seek mercy for others. Division, the sefer says, is complete falsehood, and the Rav calls these great foundations.

title.en: Each shevet with its own gate and nusach

summary.en: The Rav calls ahavas chaverim the foundation of the Ba'al Shem Tov's path, then explains the passuk of appointing judges 'for your tribes': each of the twelve shevatim has its own gate in heaven and its own nusach and halachic ways, as Sefardim and Ashkenazim differ today. He tells of Rav Chaim Ozer advising a man to move to Eretz Yisroel because of such a difference, and concludes that each kehillah has its own ways from its root at Matan Torah.

title.en: One root of the soul; brachos for the beis medrash

summary.en: The Rav says that when Providence makes people friends it is a sign they share a root of the soul, and between them love must be stronger, as he cites from the Arizal. He closes with brachos that the beis medrash be a 'bayis gadol' for Torah, tefillah and love of friends and of all Jews, and with the hope of the rebuilt Beis Hamikdash.

catalogTitle: דרשה לנשים: חשיבות מסירת נפש בזמננו

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that in a time of crisis before the redemption, Hashem withholds the means for mitzvos like hachnasas kallah so that they are done with mesiras nefesh, the one weapon the Satan cannot stop, which will bring Mashiach.

abstract.en: Speaking at a gathering for hachnasas kallah, the Rav opens with the pattern that the hardest stretch of exile comes just before the redemption: in Egypt, and in the time of Mordechai and Esther, when Haman's decree came seventy days before the miracle. He compares this to the present: Iran, the ancient Paras, threatens the Jews like a second Haman, and the economic crisis leaves people in despair and unable to help the many who ask. Why, he asks, does Hashem not give the money for the mitzvos He wants? Through the story of Yehuda and Tamar he shows that the Satan fights every opening for Mashiach, and that mesiras nefesh is the one weapon against him. Lot was saved by guests he took in with mesiras nefesh. Mesiras nefesh means acting against one's own will for Hashem, and now is the time for mitzvos done that way.

en: The hardest part of an exile comes right before the redemption, as in Egypt and in the days of Purim.
Hashem runs the world with hashgacha pratis, and the lack of money for tzedakah and hachnasas kallah is His doing, like Pharaoh's decree of bricks without straw.
The Satan works hardest to stop Mashiach, and the one weapon he cannot defeat is mesiras nefesh.
Yehuda's immediate admission to Tamar and Lot's hospitality were acts of mesiras nefesh that saved the line of Mashiach and saved Lot.
Mesiras nefesh does not only mean being killed; it means acting against one's own will for Hashem, and in these times mitzvos must be done that way.

candidateTopics: the Satan and the coming of Mashiach

title.en: The darkest hour before the redemption

summary.en: Opening at a gathering for hachnasas kallah, the Rav describes how Pharaoh made the labor unbearable just before the Exodus, and how Haman's decree came seventy days before the Purim miracle. These, he says, were history-making days.

title.en: Iran, the economy, and a hard question

summary.en: The Rav compares the present to Purim: Iran, once Paras, threatens the Jews like a second Haman, and he hopes for a repeat of the miracle there. He describes the despair over parnassa and the constant appeals, and asks why Hashem, who wants us to give and to marry off our children, does not give the money for it.

title.en: Yehuda's admission: mesiras nefesh in a moment

summary.en: The Rav retells the episode of Yehuda and Tamar and explains that Yehuda's admission, 'she is more righteous than I', was great mesiras nefesh, made instantly because the fire had already been lit. He then asks why Tamar did not simply reveal openly that she was carrying Yehuda's children.

title.en: The one weapon against the Satan

summary.en: The Rav answers that the Satan, who will be destroyed when Mashiach comes, caused Er and Onan to sin; the only weapon against him is mesiras nefesh, so Tamar arranged that both she and Yehuda would have it. He adds that Lot was saved from Sodom because Hashem sent him guests, whom he took in with mesiras nefesh.

title.en: Hashem's present: tzedakah with mesiras nefesh

summary.en: The Rav says Mashiach must come now, but the Satan holds him back, so Hashem sends a present as He did to Lot: needy people and fathers of kallahs, while the givers have only a little, so that giving takes mesiras nefesh. He tells of a tzaddik in Yerushalayim who collected for the poor again and again, and explained that the doctor prescribed a spoonful every hour.

title.en: What mesiras nefesh means today

summary.en: The Rav defines mesiras nefesh as going against one's own will for Hashem, from the word nefesh in parshas Chayei Sarah, with examples from buying clothing and from helping kallahs. He brings the Gemara that the one who reviews the 101st time is the true oved Hashem, and closes with a brachah for the final redemption.

catalogTitle: סדרות מחוברים During ספירה - A Time for Unity Between Different Sects of Jews

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that combined sedras are the Torah's way of showing achdus among the separate groups of Klal Yisrael, that all strife grows from jealousy rooted in the moon's complaint against the sun, and why in a leap year the sedras of Sefirah stay apart.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the idea that every Jew draws from a particular letter of the Sefer Torah, which explains why people differ and why some tzaddikim are beyond imitation. Families, neighborhoods and communities mirror the Torah's words, columns, sedras and sefarim, and each Shabbos is woven from its own sedra, so sedras may not be mixed. Yet sometimes two sedras are joined: at certain times of year, before Nisan, before Tishrei, in the Three Weeks and in Sefirah, the separate groups must show ahavas chinam. Using the dispute between shlishi and shishi and the Midrash of the Yam Suf, he shows that machlokes comes from kinah, whose root is the moon's jealousy of the sun. Mashiach will end it, as hinted in Rosh Chodesh, Kiddush Levana and David and Yehonasan. A leap year, when the moon catches up with the sun, needs no combined sedras in Sefirah. He closes asking for Torah, shalom and erasing kinah.

en: Every Jew draws from a particular letter of the Sefer Torah, and people who share a root are joined as a family, a neighborhood or a community, just as letters form words, columns, sedras and sefarim.
Each Shabbos is woven from the letters of its own sedra, so sedras may not be mixed; when two are joined it is to show achdus among separate groups.
The sedras are joined at times that call for ahavas chinam: before Nisan and Tishrei, in the Three Weeks, and in Sefirah when the students of Rabbi Akiva did not show each other honor.
All machlokes and all the troubles of history come from kinah, jealousy, and kinah breeds sinah, hatred.
The root of kinah is the moon's jealousy of the sun, and when Mashiach comes the moon will be restored and kinah will be removed from the world.
A leap year, in which the moon catches up with the sun, is itself a sign of the moon's repair, so its Sefirah weeks need no combined sedras as a reminder.
